Under any interior exponential tilt, mean convergence and O(epsilon) variance give the full open-set lower bound; exponential Markov inequalities, finite covers, and exponential tightness give the closed-set upper bound. Differentiated series determine the unique saddle, and local/large amplitude expansions are derived with explicit parameter domains. value.rationale: The source problem explicitly contrasts a near-Gaussian weak-resetting stationary center with exponential tails; the rate of exponentially rare stationary excursions at the natural inverse-gap scale is not fixed by either central convergence or fixed-gap tail formulas. The theorem gives a full probability LDP, an exact special-function rate with provable strict departure from Gaussian cost, sharp quadratic-to-linear crossover and finite-epsilon pressure enclosure. Such an asymptotic is a natural experimentally measurable precision benchmark, not a routine parameter substitution, isolated normalization check, or arbitrary finite table.
